youtube.title: The Count of Traded Wildlife Just Doubled
youtube.description:
A new study counts at least 107,356 wild species used or traded worldwide: how many species are traded, and what the number does not say.

Reported from 29 Oct to 3 Nov 2026. A study in Science Advances puts the count of wild species used or traded at 107,356, more than double the roughly 50,000 of an earlier intergovernmental assessment. This explainer shows what was counted (animals, plants and fungi), why the new figure is a broader count and not proof that trade doubled, where the gaps in the data are, and what the authors propose. It also says plainly what is still unknown.

Question for the comments: Which gap in the data should be closed first?

Sources (read 15 Nov 2026):
- University of Sheffield release, 29 Oct 2026: https://sheffield.ac.uk/news/global-wildlife-trade-involves-more-double-number-species-previously-estimated
- Down To Earth, 3 Nov 2026: https://www.downtoearth.org.in/wildlife-biodiversity/global-wildlife-trade-involves-more-than-107000-species-twice-previous-estimates-study
- Queen Mary University of London release: https://www.qmul.ac.uk/news/latest-news/2026/science-and-engineering/se/global-wildlife-trade-involves-more-than-100000-species-new-study-reveals.html
If a figure here is out of date, the sources above are the reference.
